assertion.en: Under First Past The Post, a party can win more than half of the seats with less than half of the votes.

reason.en: Each constituency goes to the candidate with the most votes there, even if that candidate has less than 50 per cent.

b.en: Both statements are true, but here the second does explain the first: small leads in many constituencies each win a whole seat.

c.en: The assertion is true. A party can win 15 of 25 seats on 40 per cent of the votes.

d.en: The reason is true. That is the rule of First Past The Post.

explanation.en: Both are true, and the reason explains the assertion. Each constituency is won on its own, so a party that leads narrowly in many of them can hold most of the seats without most of the votes.

hints.en: Think of a party that comes first in 15 of 25 constituencies with about 40 per cent in each.
